comments.body:
RCA (rebar-debug Phase 1 — proven, runtime-confirmed). Disposition: ESCALATE (fix requires a design decision on the error-code vocabulary; no code changed).

PROVEN ROOT CAUSE (corrects this ticket's stated Mechanism)
The two cited reproductions (render_workflow, get_workflow_status) do NOT go through
`_mcp_llm._structured_llm_failure`. Those are READ_ONLY tools in `_mcp_reads.py` with no
try/except; their exceptions flow through the GENERIC MCP error guard
`_mcp_errors._envelope_error` -> `rebar._errors.error_code_for`. The real mechanism:

- `WorkflowError` and `WorkflowParseError` (src/rebar/llm/errors.py:114-118) are declared
  subclasses of `LLMError`. They are the workflow engine's DSL parse/lint/migrate/execute/
  lookup error base -- NOT availability errors.
- `render_workflow("nonexistent-wf")` raises `WorkflowParseError("... not found ...")`
  (runs.py:85); `get_workflow_status("nonexistent-run")` raises
  `WorkflowError("unknown run_id ...")` (runs.py:515).
- `error_code_for` (src/rebar/_errors.py:141-142) has a blanket branch 6:
  `isinstance(exc, LLMError) -> "llm_unavailable"`. These workflow errors set no
  `error_code` attribute, so branch 5 does not fire and every workflow caller-input/
  not-found error collapses to `llm_unavailable`.

PROOF (runtime, worktree at origin/main dddaa606):
    render_workflow  -> error_code_for = llm_unavailable
      envelope: {'error':'llm_unavailable','input':'','message':"nonexistent-wf: workflow
                 'nonexistent-wf' not found ..."}
    get_workflow_status -> error_code_for = llm_unavailable
      envelope: {'error':'llm_unavailable','input':'','message':"unknown run_id
                 'nonexistent-run': no run-index entry and no ticket_id given"}
These envelopes match the ticket's reproductions exactly. The MCP envelope shape is
{error,input,message} (no resolution_class/retryable/diagnostic) -- confirming the path is
error_code_for, not _structured_llm_failure. `_structured_llm_failure` is a SECOND,
independent hard-coded `"error":"llm_unavailable"` site (used by review_code/verify_completion/
review_plan); it shares the defect class but is not the path for the two cited repros.

DEFECT ORIGIN (caused_by): ticket 8a31 = biomedical-upper-tench (8a31-e1c3-cf31-4239),
commit 77f1c4011c83 "8a31: MCP failures get CLI's structured error id". That change created
the structured-MCP-error obligation and shipped `error_code_for` with the blanket
`LLMError -> llm_unavailable` mapping without carving out the workflow caller-input/not-found
subclasses (its own message even notes "_mcp_reads/_mcp_llm: the two return-shaped soft errors
gain a code"). Close-class: plan_defect.

LEGITIMACY: defect (standing intent). The structured-identity contract
(docs/mcp-reference.md "Failure shape": `error` drawn from `rebar.KNOWN_ERROR_CODES`) is set
by biomedical-upper-tench; wolflike-chevroned-haddock and dear-name-ladle are the same
"non-availability failure misclassified as llm_unavailable" defect class, both closed fixed.

WHY ESCALATE (not auto-fix). Satisfying AC1/AC2/AC4 requires ADDING new member(s) to the
exported `rebar.KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` vocabulary (also common.schema.json + docs/mcp-reference.md
"Failure shape") -- a contract/schema/API surface change -- and a genuine taxonomy tradeoff:
`WorkflowError` is the base for parse/lint/migrate/EXECUTE errors, and a workflow execution
step can genuinely fail on LLM unavailability, so a blanket `WorkflowError -> not_found` would
regress AC3. The correct design (which new code name(s): workflow_not_found vs not_found vs
invalid_input; whether to introduce finer-grained not-found/caller-input exception subtypes or
set `error_code` attrs on just the not-found/parse sites; and whether `_structured_llm_failure`
should derive its code from error_code_for) is a new design decision. No ADR prescribes it.

SIBLINGS/RESIDUAL: `_structured_llm_failure` (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:21-37) hard-codes
`llm_unavailable` for the LLM-tier tools; the same fix should route it through the chosen
classification so AC4 holds there too. No fix landed; no worktree retained beyond this session.

## Phase 2 complete — RED→GREEN fix implemented, committed (Change-Id I5ecbef2, local HEAD c2505ef96cb2), pushing to Gerrit

**Problem (confirmed).** The read-only MCP tools `render_workflow` and `get_workflow_status` returned `error:"llm_unavailable"` for caller-input / not-found cases. Root cause (per Phase-1 RCA): the WorkflowError subtree subclasses LLMError, and `error_code_for` (_errors.py) blanket-mapped every LLMError → llm_unavailable. A second hard-coded site existed at `_structured_llm_failure` (_mcp_llm.py).

**Proof (held-out oracle).** Added tests/interfaces/contracts/test_workflow_error_codes_dbca.py (7 tests) driving the ACTUAL MCP read tools and `error_code_for`. Confirmed RED for the right reasons before the fix; GREEN after. A sandboxed mutation check (seed the defect back) returned the 4 behaviour tests to RED and left the 3 base-guard tests green; restoring the fix returned all green.

**Fix (per-subclass, NOT a blanket flip).**
- Added `not_found` + `invalid_input` to the exported `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` (schemas/common.schema.json + docs/mcp-reference.md + regenerated tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json).
- New `WorkflowNotFoundError(WorkflowError)` raised at the 4 not-found sites in runs.py (unknown workflow name; unknown run_id; run absent from ticket ×2) → `not_found`. Optional `source=` kwarg preserves the `<name>: workflow '<name>' not found ...` message shape.
- WorkflowParseError / WorkflowValidationError / WorkflowVersionError (found but won't parse/lint/migrate) → `invalid_input`.
- The bare `WorkflowError` base (the EXECUTE base) DELIBERATELY still maps to `llm_unavailable` — an execute step can genuinely fail on LLM outage. **AC3 protected.**
- Classifier logic centralised in `error_code_for` via extracted `_workflow_caller_code` helper (keeps McCabe ≤15, no baseline bump). `_structured_llm_failure` now delegates to `error_code_for` so both LLM-tier sites share one taxonomy.

**Defect origin (caused_by, confirmed).** Same class as the Phase-1 finding: the blanket LLMError→llm_unavailable mapping introduced in 8a31-e1c3-cf31-4239 (biomedical-upper-tench, commit 77f1c4011c83). Close class: plan_defect (same as closed fixes wolflike-chevroned-haddock, dear-name-ladle).

**Scope & safety.** Caller-dependency sweep: the only `except WorkflowParseError` catchers (schema.py, lint.py) are on the parse-text path, which the name-resolution not-found does not traverse; CLI catches broad WorkflowError; `pytest.raises(WorkflowError, match=...)` in test_workflow_entrypoints.py still holds because WorkflowNotFoundError IS-A WorkflowError. Regression: full sweep tests/unit/workflow/ + tests/interfaces/contracts/ + test_workflow_entrypoints + llm failure matrix = 1172 passed; targeted envelope/render/api-surface = 46 passed. make lint (incl. complexity baseline new=0 increased=0) + make typecheck (683 files) clean.

**Siblings (escalated, NOT fixed — needed a new design decision).** Two more bare-WorkflowError sites still collapse to llm_unavailable: executor.py:541 (unknown scripted step) and editor.py:475 (missing editor bundle). Filed as fightable-nirvanic-kitten (35ab-f0e0-3e4a-4b72), linked discovered_from this ticket. Left out of scope per operator direction to escalate new error-code design decisions.

**Residual risk.** Low. Vocabulary additions are additive/backward-compatible; the reclassification is confined to the WorkflowError subtree via a dedicated not-found subclass, with execute-time outages provably preserved.

**Replication.** Original report no longer reproduces end-to-end: both `render_workflow` (unknown name) and `get_workflow_status` (unknown run_id) now return `not_found` through the real MCP tools.

Next: push to Gerrit; await LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1; Submit; then close with --class=plan_defect --caused-by=8a31-e1c3-cf31-4239.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Every LLM-tier MCP tool failure is reported with the single error code `llm_unavailable`,
including failures that have nothing to do with LLM availability. A driving agent that
branches on the error code — which is exactly what the structured failure exists for — cannot
tell "the model backend is down, retry later" from "you named a workflow that does not exist,
fix your input".

Observed 2026-08-27 against the LIVE MCP server (`https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp`),
where `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM=1` and the LLM tier is fully enabled:

```
render_workflow    {"workflow": "nonexistent-wf"}
  -> {"error": "llm_unavailable",
      "message": "nonexistent-wf: workflow 'nonexistent-wf' not found (no such file,
                  no .rebar/workflows/nonexistent-wf.yaml, and no built-in example of that name)"}

get_workflow_status {"run_id": "nonexistent-run"}
  -> {"error": "llm_unavailable",
      "message": "unknown run_id 'nonexistent-run': no run-index entry and no ticket_id given"}
```

Both are caller-input errors on tools documented as always-available reads that make no LLM
call at all (`render_workflow`: "Read tool, always available"; `get_workflow_status`: "Typed
read tool ... (no execution)"). Neither is an availability problem, and neither is retryable in
the sense the field implies.

## Mechanism
`src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:21-37`

```python
def _structured_llm_failure(exc: Exception) -> dict:
    ...
    o = outcome_of(exc)
    return {
        "error": "llm_unavailable",
        "message": str(exc),
        "resolution_class": o.resolution_class.value if o is not None else None,
        "retryable": bool(o.retryable) if o is not None else False,
        "diagnostic": o.diagnostic if o is not None else None,
    }
```

The `error` code is a hard-coded literal applied to every `LLMError` the tier raises,
regardless of cause. When the raised error carries no classifier outcome (`outcome_of`
returns `None`) — which is the case for a not-found lookup — the caller additionally gets
`resolution_class: null`, `retryable: false`, `diagnostic: null`, so there is no other field
to disambiguate from either. The docstring's stated purpose ("The driving agent can then
branch on `retryable` ... instead of string-parsing an error") is defeated: string-parsing
`message` is the only way to recover the real cause.

## Impact
The MCP failure contract (`docs/mcp-reference.md`, "Failure shape") promises a
machine-readable identity drawn from `rebar.KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` that lets a client tell a
policy refusal from a fault. For the LLM tier that promise does not hold: an unrecoverable
caller mistake and a transient backend outage are indistinguishable without natural-language
parsing, so an agent will either retry a permanently-broken call or escalate a typo.

## Reproduction
1. Against an MCP server with `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM=1`, call `render_workflow` with a workflow
   name that does not exist.
2. Observe `error: "llm_unavailable"` with `resolution_class: null`, `retryable: false`.
3. Repeat with `get_workflow_status` and an unknown `run_id`; observe the same code.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: A not-found workflow name from `render_workflow` returns an error code distinct from `llm_unavailable` that identifies it as a caller-input/not-found error.
- [ ] AC2: An unknown `run_id` from `get_workflow_status` likewise returns a not-found error code, not `llm_unavailable`.
- [ ] AC3: A genuine LLM backend unavailability (no API key, or a provider error) still returns `llm_unavailable` with the classifier fields populated.
- [ ] AC4: Every error code emitted by `_structured_llm_failure` is a member of `rebar.KNOWN_ERROR_CODES`, matching the failure-shape contract in `docs/mcp-reference.md`.
- [ ] AC5: Regression tests cover AC1, AC2, and AC3 — asserting on the `error` code, not the message text.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] DD1: AC1-AC4 implemented; AC5 tests pass.
- [ ] DD2: `docs/mcp-reference.md` failure-shape section names the LLM-tier codes if the set changes.

## Fix Plan (operator-approved — dbca-97ac-ad96-4d6d)

Corrects the ticket's stated Mechanism per the proven RCA: the two cited reproductions flow
through the GENERIC MCP guard `_mcp_errors._envelope_error` -> `rebar._errors.error_code_for`
(NOT `_structured_llm_failure`). `error_code_for` (src/rebar/_errors.py) blanket-maps every
`LLMError` -> `llm_unavailable` at branch 6, and `WorkflowError`/`WorkflowParseError`
(subclasses of `LLMError`) collapse there. A second, independent hard-coded site is
`_structured_llm_failure` (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py), used by the LLM-tier execute tools.

Approach (per-subclass, NOT a blanket flip — protects AC3):
1. Vocabulary: add `not_found` and `invalid_input` to `rebar.KNOWN_ERROR_CODES`
   (src/rebar/_errors.py), mirrored into `docs/mcp-reference.md` (Failure shape) and the
   `common.schema.json` error-field description. Additive / backward-compatible.
2. New exception `WorkflowNotFoundError(WorkflowError)` (src/rebar/llm/errors.py) for the
   caller-input NOT-FOUND lookup misses only: unknown workflow name (runs.py:85), unknown
   run_id (runs.py:515), run-not-found-on-ticket (runs.py:527/548). Message text preserved
   (optional `source=` prefix). It is a `WorkflowError` so the broad CLI `except WorkflowError`
   and the `pytest.raises(WorkflowError, match="unknown run_id")` entrypoint test still hold.
3. `error_code_for`: new branch BEFORE the LLMError branch —
   `WorkflowNotFoundError` -> `not_found`; `WorkflowParseError`/`WorkflowValidationError`/
   `WorkflowVersionError` -> `invalid_input`. The BARE `WorkflowError` base is left on the
   LLMError branch -> `llm_unavailable`, because a workflow EXECUTE step can genuinely fail on
   LLM unavailability (AC3). Per-subclass, never a base remap.
4. `_structured_llm_failure` derives `error` from `error_code_for(exc)` instead of the literal,
   keeping the LLM tier consistent with the taxonomy while genuine outages
   (`LLMUnavailableError` etc.) still resolve to `llm_unavailable`. Disposition fields
   (`resolution_class`/`retryable`/`diagnostic`) unchanged.
5. Held-out regression tests exercise the ACTUAL MCP read tools (render_workflow,
   get_workflow_status) and assert on the `error` CODE (not message): AC1 not_found, AC2
   not_found, AC3 bare-WorkflowError/LLMUnavailable -> llm_unavailable, AC4 membership.

Caller-dependency sweep: the `except WorkflowParseError` catchers (schema.py, lint.py) sit on
the parse-text path, which the name-resolution not-found (`_resolve_source_path`) does not
traverse; CLI catches the broad `WorkflowError`. Only-incidental usage -> safe to proceed.

Out-of-scope siblings (bare `WorkflowError` at executor.py:541 "unknown scripted step" and
editor.py:475 "missing editor bundle" also collapse to `llm_unavailable`): filed as a
discovered_from follow-up rather than expanded here (each needs a NEW code decision).

file_impact.reason: Add not_found + invalid_input to KNOWN_ERROR_CODES; add per-subclass WorkflowError-subtree mapping in error_code_for (before the LLMError branch)
Add WorkflowNotFoundError(WorkflowError) subclass for name/run/run_id lookup misses, distinct from parse/lint and from the execute base
Retarget the not-found raise sites (workflow name, unknown run_id, run-not-found-on-ticket) to WorkflowNotFoundError, preserving message text
Route _structured_llm_failure error code through error_code_for so the LLM-tier tools honour the new taxonomy instead of hard-coding llm_unavailable
Document not_found + invalid_input in the error_envelope error-field description
Document the LLM-tier/workflow not_found + invalid_input codes in the Failure shape section
Regenerated public-surface baseline reflecting the two new KNOWN_ERROR_CODES members
New held-out regression tests: per-class error code through the actual MCP read tools (AC1/AC2), execute-base still llm_unavailable (AC3), vocabulary membership (AC4)
